identityReview: Chrystia Freeland, Canadian former deputy prime minister and finance minister, born 2 August 1968 according to the Canadian Press profile. Currently Warden of Rhodes House and CEO of the Rhodes Trust, not an MP or head of the University of Oxford. Canadian reconstruction representative and Ukrainian presidential economic adviser are separate appointments. An unverified expanded birth name is not added as an alias.
lifeStatusEvidence: The Rhodes Trust reports her actual start on 1 July 2026 and quotes her as current Warden and CEO in its 13 November 2026 report about a gift announced on 7 November. This supports current institutional activity and role, without claiming that the quotation proves her physical attendance at the 7 November event.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read current and dated Rhodes Trust pages; the Canadian Press profile; Columbia’s explicitly historical biography; Commons role tables; Canadian Order in Council; Reuters reporting on the Ukrainian advisory appointment and 2024 resignation; archived Canadian appointment announcement; the introduction to CUSMA implementation guidance; and publisher edition metadata. Read Commons image provenance, licensing declaration and crop history.
corrections: Read the current Rhodes House Warden biography. It identifies Freeland as an Alberta-born Rhodes Scholar who came to Oxford in 1991 and describes her earlier journalism and editorial work at the Financial Times, Globe and Mail and Thomson Reuters. The 1991 date is her arrival as a scholar, not an inferred graduation date. A 2023 Northeastern honorary degree is not treated as an earned doctorate. Historical media jobs are not current appointments.

Read Dylan Robertson’s Canadian Press profile dated 19 January 2025, republished by CollingwoodToday. It gives birth on 2 August 1968 in Peace River, Alberta; earlier education and journalism; election in 2013; and appointment as Canada’s first woman federal finance minister in 2020. Its leadership-candidate context belongs to January 2025 and is not a current leadership office. Pandemic spending is government policy, not a personal causal claim about all economic outcomes. Family details are unnecessary and omitted.

Read Columbia World Leaders Forum biography, explicitly sourced to April 2007. It establishes a Harvard bachelor’s degree in history and literature and a Master of Studies at St Antony’s College, Oxford. Neither degree’s graduation year is stated. MSt is retained by its actual degree name, not reclassified as a doctorate or a research-only degree. Its then-current FT position and New York residence are historical, despite the website’s 2026 footer. The page’s first-book title variant is not reused.

Read the House of Commons roles tables. Toronto Centre service began 25 November 2013; University—Rosedale service began 19 October 2015 and ended 9 January 2026. The table lists Finance from 18 August 2020 and Deputy Prime Minister from 20 November 2019, both ending 15 December 2024; the public resignation announcement on 16 December is recorded separately. Transport and Internal Trade ran from 14 March to 16 September 2025, split into rows at the new parliament rather than a gap in service. Special Representative for the Reconstruction of Ukraine, listed as a parliamentary-secretary role, ran 16 September 2025 to 5 January 2026. She is no longer an MP. These Canadian offices are distinct from advising the Ukrainian president.

Read the Rhodes Trust release of 1 July 2026, explicitly stating that she starts today as Warden of Rhodes House and CEO of the Trust. She succeeds interim Warden/CEO Sir Rick Trainor, who had served since 1 January 2025 and remains as Provost. Do not describe her as merely incoming after July, as directly succeeding Elizabeth Kiss, or as head of the University of Oxford. The Trust is a scholarship charity.

Read the Rhodes Trust report published 13 November 2026. Kevin Xu’s gift was announced at the fifth Tech & Society Forum on 7 November; it extends a partnership begun in 2022 through 2030. The report quotes Freeland as current Warden and CEO. Abhilash Mishra conceived the gathering and developed it with Trust leadership; Xu funded its launch. Do not credit her with founding the Forum, making the gift or delivering all future results. Her quotation establishes a dated institutional statement, not independent proof of physical attendance on 7 November.

Read Order in Council P.C. 2026-0001, dated 9 January 2026. It terminates her parliamentary-secretary appointment effective 5 January 2026, referring to appointment P.C. 2025-0661 of 16 September 2025. The order’s publication/signature date is distinct from its effective date and from the MP term ending on 9 January. Cross-check with the Commons role label rather than treating every appointment involving Ukraine as the same office.

Read Reuters’ 5 January 2026 report, including Zelenskiy’s appointment announcement and Freeland’s statement that she would advise on economic development without pay. It then described her MP departure as future; the Commons record subsequently confirms 9 January. Retain the January appointment as historical, not an independently verified continuing November advisory mandate. The Ukrainian presidential decree page could not be read beyond navigation before repeated timeouts, so no assertion of full decree inspection or its precise legal category is made.

Read the archived Canadian prime ministerial release of 18 August 2020. It appoints Freeland to Finance while retaining her Deputy Prime Minister office and notes her role in NAFTA renegotiation and the government’s COVID response. Recovery language is a prospective remit, not evidence that particular economic outcomes had already been achieved. Bill Morneau’s earlier measures are not reassigned to Freeland.

Read the contemporaneous Reuters report of 16 December 2024 as republished by Kitco, including the relevant paragraphs on the fiscal-update schedule, spending disagreement, possible US tariffs and resignation letter. Her assessment of spending and tariff risks is explicitly attributed, not adopted as a finding of policy failure or corruption. Retain the public announcement date alongside the Commons table’s 15 December term endpoint. This historical story does not establish Trudeau or other officials’ current offices.

Read the introduction and purpose section of Global Affairs Canada’s CUSMA Statement on Implementation. It distinguishes signature on 30 November 2018, amendment on 10 December 2019, completion notices in April 2020 and entry into force on 1 July 2020. Combine treaty chronology with the prime ministerial biography for her negotiating involvement. Preserve the collective roles of three governments and negotiating teams; do not identify her as sole author or assume signature itself brought the agreement into force. Government claims of expected benefits are not independent measurements; the full chapter-by-chapter legal text was not reviewed.

Read Simon & Schuster Canada’s product details and author description for Unreliable Boyfriend, hardcover ISBN 9781668245903. The listed publication date is 13 October 2026, distinct from earlier book announcements and from possible other editions. The bibliographic claim is limited to this edition. The book itself was not read; publisher promotional judgments and endorsement blurbs are not independent assessments. Earlier editorial employment is cross-checked against Rhodes and Columbia biographies.

sourceReview.limits: Eight-language content is AI-reviewed, not certified by native-language human editors. No full-book reading, full treaty legal analysis or audiovisual inspection. Ukrainian appointment is verified through Reuters, not the unread decree. November Trust quotation is not proof of event attendance. Portrait source-gallery access, original bytes and visual review remain outstanding.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English. Preserve 1 July actual start versus earlier incoming wording; Trust leadership versus Oxford university leadership; degree titles versus honorary degrees and unverified graduation years; Canadian special representative versus Ukrainian adviser; order date versus effective date and MP endpoint; 16 December resignation announcement versus 15 December parliamentary table endpoint; treaty signature versus amendment versus entry into force; 13 November report versus 7 November gift announcement; future support to 2030 versus completed results; and publisher edition metadata versus a review of the book.
